title: compact request serialization and elide thread pin operations
author: Ethan Brooks
description: Motivation: p99 CPU time in the request path is dominated by short-lived heap allocations, repeated mutex acquisitions around small critical sections, and unnecessary thread pin/unpin operations when a request briefly touches the KV cache. This causes higher latency variance and worsens throughput under tail loads. This PR introduces a compact, copy-once serialization path and a tiered workerpool that avoids pinning for the common fast path. Key changes: 1) Introduce a bump-arena allocator (serve/alloc/bump_arena.{h,cpp}) used for per-request scratch during parsing/serialization to eliminate many small heap allocations; arenas are recycled to avoid lifetime bookkeeping. 2) Add a compact wire serializer (serve/serialization/compact_serializer.{h,cpp}) that writes into a single contiguous buffer using size-prefixed records; this reduces memcpy churn and makes kernel selection deterministic for small requests. 3) Convert the global worker pool to a two-tier model (serve/worker/tiered_pool.{h,cpp}): a hot pool of pinned long-running threads for large KV-cache/streaming workloads and a fast-ephemeral pool of unpinned workers for short requests. 4) Replace a couple of high-contention std::mutex-protected queues with a lock-free handover queue used for passing request ownership between IO and worker threads. 5) Add KV-access hints so tiny cache lookups avoid a full thread handover: the IO thread can perform a single inline probe against a read-only snapshot when the probe is O(1). Backwards compatibility and safety: the bump arena is strictly scoped to the request cycle; compact serializer falls back to the previous path when an object exceeds the compact buffer threshold. Benchmarks: on internal continuous_batching_test and a replay of production traces, median latency improved by 9-12% and p99 improved by 18-24% under 95th percentile load. CPU utilization dropped ~7% for the same QPS. Rollout: staged canary on dedicated pools (10% -> 50% -> 100%) with automatic rollback on latency regressions >5% for p99 or error rate increases. Migration plan: feature-flagged behind runtime.config.experimental.compact_serialize; default off for first week. Checklist: - [x] bump arena implementation and tests - [x] compact serializer + tests - [x] tiered workerpool + integration tests - [x] lock-free handover queue impl and unit tests - [x] perf benchmarks and docs - [x] feature flag and canary rollout plan References: internal doc https://linear.app/ENG/issue/ENG-1024, perf notes in repo at docs/notes/perf-2026-02-10.md

review_comments: Asha Patel: Nice approach. Two asks before approving: (1) can the bump arena be diagnostics-enabled so we can track high-water usage per request? (2) please add a comment explaining the memory ownership contract between IO thread and ephemeral worker when using handover queue.
Author (Ethan): Added arena high-water counter behind a metrics flag and expanded comments in handover_queue.h to describe ownership and when a deep copy is required.

Connor Li: I ran the perf workload twice and saw one outlier p99 regression on a large-batched workload. I suspect the pinned hot-pool is starving ephemeral workers under extreme load. Can we add backpressure from hot-pool to the IO thread?
Author (Ethan): Added a soft backpressure token bucket that prevents the hot-pool from stealing more than N tokens per second; updated tests and added config knobs. Re-ran perf, outlier disappeared.
Marisol Vega: Minor: thread naming for the hot-pinned threads would help in flamegraphs. Also add a lint exception justification for the aligned_alloc usage.
Author (Ethan): Renamed threads to include pool and role, added lint rationale comment. All reviewers approved in the final review.

release_notes: Introduces an opt-in compact request serialization and a tiered workerpool to reduce CPU overhead in the request path. Expect latency and CPU utilization improvements; feature is behind runtime.config.experimental.compact_serialize. Rollout will be gradual with canary and automatic rollback on regressions.
